items.title: a service's CONTRACT HASH reads its annotations AS WRITTEN, so a type ALIAS and its target hash apart: a whole-value `[expose]` or an `[rpc]` signature spelled `Map<..>` (the deprecated alias) and one spelled `HashMap<..>` get different hashes for the same wire contract (the plain twin's pin moved c63e39e3 → d093c571)
items.discussion: collections-44 (Order 44, I9 @0a4ab701); rpc.vl's `[service]` expansion; keyed exposures hash the value type and did not move
items.body: A client and server built from the same source still agree, so nothing breaks today; but a client rebuilt after a respelling reads as a contract change it is not. Rec: hash the RESOLVED type (aliases expanded) — the contract is the wire shape, not the spelling. Sizing S; std/rpc + the analyzer's type printer, Order 45.

items.title: the import steer indexes only DECLARED names, so an unimported `Map`/`Set` (now a deprecated alias import in `std::map`/`std::set`) gets NO hint, while an unimported `HashMap` gets the right one
items.body: Index an exported alias import (`export … import … as Map`) as the name it binds, pointing at the new name (the deprecation text): 'did you mean `HashMap` (std::hash_map)? `Map` is its deprecated alias'. Sizing S; solver or editor, Order 45.
